the oral administration of colitic protein extracts can ameliorate DSS-induced colonic inflammation and that this is associated with an increased proportion of intestinal γδ T cells.

the role of oral tolerance in the prevention and treatment of IBD.
the potential role of oral colitis proteins in the induction of oral tolerance and the relative role of intestinal mucosal γγ T cells in the development of colitis in a mouse model.
the role of γδ T cells during oral tolerance induction in a murine colitis model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protective effect of oral tolerance on colitis is related to the increase of large intestinal mucosa γδ T cells.
γδ T cells are involved in the protective effect of oral administration of colonic proteins.

oral tolerance to colitis-extracted protein is associated with an increased number of γδ T cells and a decreased number of Th1 cytokine-producing cells in large intestinal lamina propria, which may contribute to the protective effect of oral tolerance on colitis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oral tolerance is an efficient approach in treating IBD and the intestinal mucosal CD8α+ γδ T cells are the key effector cells in the process of mucosal healing.
oral administration of CEP could be a promising therapy for IBD.
the increase in γδT cells in large intestinal lymphocytes may be one of the mechanisms of the protective effect of oral administration of colitic proteins in DSS-induced colitic mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oral tolerance can be achieved in a murine DSS-induced colitic model.
oral administration of colitic proteins can ameliorate colitis by inducing an increase in intestinal mucosal γ/δ T cell populations.
oral colitis-extraced proteins may be used as a novel therapy for IBD.
